approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US 2 west about 31 miles, turn right onto Smithbrook Road (Forest Road 6700) and go about 3 miles to the trailhead on the left. Forest Road 6700 is closed to vehicles by a storm-damage order from May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027, unless lifted sooner.

pins.name: Smithbrook Trailhead
pins.note: End of FR 6700 gravel spur off US-2 near milepost 68; Northwest Forest Pass required, self-issue wilderness permit at the kiosk.
pins.directions: From US-2 near milepost 68, turn onto Smithbrook Road (FR 6700), a gravel spur, and follow it about 3 miles to the Smithbrook Trailhead at roughly 4,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and you self-issue the wilderness permit at the kiosk here. Smithbrook Road is unplowed in winter and typically melts out by early to mid summer; attempt it before the road opens and you add about two miles of snow-road walking each way.

pins.name: Smithbrook Trail / PCT junction
pins.note: Smithbrook Trail #1590 tops out at the Pacific Crest Trail; turn left (south) toward Lake Valhalla.

pins.name: Lake Valhalla, south tip
pins.note: Where the PCT bends southwest away from the lake, drop off-trail down a steep dirt path to the water and follow rocky shoreline to the south tip to leave the maintained trail.

pins.name: Base of southeast boulder slope
pins.note: Past the lake's south tip, boulder-hop southeast until Lichtenberg's southeast shoulder comes into view and a class 2 line up to the ridge is visible.

pins.name: Southeast gully / talus slope
pins.note: Loose rock and shifting talus on the class 2 climb to the ridgeline; test holds and watch for parties below.

pins.name: Ridge gain point east of true summit
pins.note: Boulder scramble tops out on the summit ridge just east of the true summit, the eastern of the mountain's two tops; turn west for the final walk to the top.

pins.name: Lichtenberg Mountain summit
pins.note: True summit overlooks Lake Valhalla to the west and Lichtenwasser Lake to the northeast; on descent retrace the ridge and gully, taking care on the loose upper talus.
